disease_label_per_paper: Ocular administration of brinzolamide leading to SJS/TEN overlap
presentation_summary: 31-year-old previously healthy man underwent pars plana vitrectomy for traumatic right retinal detachment, then developed secondary glaucoma and started topical brinzolamide 1% twice daily on postoperative day 18.

On day 6 of brinzolamide use he developed high fever up to 40 C and erythematous rash on both upper limbs, rapidly progressing to widespread edematous erythema, flaccid bullae, coalescing blisters, epidermal detachment, and erosions.
Initial epidermal detachment area was 20%, progressing to over 80% within 24 hours; abstract reports erosions involving 99% TBSA. Nikolsky sign was positive.

Mucosal erosions and exudation involved lips, eyelids, oral mucosa, and perineum; ocular involvement was asymmetric with right eyelid ulceration/conjunctival hyperemia and severe left conjunctival chemosis plus corneal epithelial detachment.

Admission labs showed WBC 3.78 x10^9/L, neutrophils 85.2%, lymphocytes 9.9%, platelets 91 x10^9/L, CRP 156.06 mg/L, ALT 57.2 IU/L, AST 49.7 IU/L, GGT 92.5 IU/L, albumin 34.4 g/L, sodium 131.03 mmol/L, and blood cultures positive for E. coli and Streptococcus.

clinical_course.event: Right-eye vitrectomy and related procedures performed for traumatic retinal detachment; postoperative topical levofloxacin, tobramycin-dexamethasone, and oral methylprednisolone used.
Postoperative day 18 secondary glaucoma diagnosed; steroid eye drops stopped and brinzolamide 1% eye drops started twice daily.
High fever to 40 C and upper-limb erythematous rash rapidly progressed to widespread bullae, erosions, multisite mucosal injury, and ocular surface disease.
Epidermal detachment progressed from 20% to over 80% within 24 hours.
Skin lesions largely healed with residual hyperpigmentation and scarring; left eye developed symblepharon and dense corneal scarring requiring penetrating keratoplasty.
